title: paged KV cache: adaptive allocator reuse & locality-aware pinning heuristic
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache has seen increased contention and suboptimal locality for multi-tenant continuous-batching workloads. This PR introduces an adaptive reuse heuristic in the block allocator and a locality-aware pinning policy to reduce copy churn, improve cache hit stability, and lower tail latencies.

Summary of changes: implemented an adaptive reuse score in the paged block allocator that favors reusing recently-evicted blocks when host/service access patterns show temporal reuse; introduced a locality-aware pinning policy that pins hot blocks preferentially on same-GPU NUMA domains and promotes co-located eviction groups to reduce cross-device transfers; added a TTL-based decay factor to pinning so long-lived but cold entries don't starve allocation; exposed tuning knobs via runtime flags and config for dedicated deployments.

Perf results (internal benchmark, text generation workload with 2k context, mix of short and long tails): median throughput +11.8%, average token latency -7.3%, p99 latency -18.5%; KV cache hit-rate improvement +6.2% on high-concurrency traces. Improvements are most visible under steady continuous-batching (50-200 reqs/s/GPU) and mixed-sequence-length workloads.

API/Config: added runtime flags --kv-allocator-adaptive-reuse=(off|on|auto), --kv-pinning-locality=(off|node|gpu), and --kv-pinning-ttl-ms to tune decay. Defaults: auto reuse, gpu locality, ttl 300000ms.

Testing: unit tests for allocator reuse scoring and pinning eviction; integration tests simulating cross-tenant traffic; e2e benchmark harness updated to include mixed-length traces used in measurements. CI includes flaky-test guard for allocator stress tests.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag (off by default in private/dedicated until validated); staged rollout to canary pool for 48h then to 25% of production traffic, monitor p99 latency, KV hit-rate, and cross-device transfer bytes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc + linear tickets referenced (ENG-4125, ENG-4310)
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks and benchmark harness updates
- [x] Runtime flags & defaults set for safe rollout

Notes: There are a handful of heuristic constants tuned against internal traces; we expose them to ops for per-customer tuning. Follow-up work: integrate with scheduler hints to prefetch blocks onto target GPUs when canary signals predict imminent reuse (tracked in ENG-4402).

review_comments: Riley Chen: Great direction, can you clarify the invariants for reuse scoring? specifically, when reuse score ties with MRU there's risk of ping-ponging between blocks.
Ethan Park: We add a small hysteresis factor (configurable via --kv-reuse-hysteresis) to break ties; updated allocator_tests to cover the ping-pong scenario.
Priya Nair: Suggest exposing the pinning-ttl in ms as we have sub-second hot/cold signals in some customers. Also add a guard to avoid pinning >80% of device memory.
Ethan Park: TTL exposed as --kv-pinning-ttl-ms. Added soft cap enforcement with a runtime override in ops config. Added integration test for cap behavior.
Marco Silva: CI flaky tests observed in allocator stress harness; can we isolate nondeterminism?
Ethan Park: Split the stress test off with a flaky guard and deterministic seed. CI now retries the stress job separately; stable unit tests unaffected.
Riley Chen: Approved after the hysteresis and TTL cap changes.
